title: Target response means improved source ranks over matched cohorts in 79 selected MICrONS axons
abstract: We tested whether the mean movie response of anatomical targets can distinguish its source from other measured sources. We used public MICrONS v1 data from one mouse. All source-template cells were excluded from target pools. The main gallery had 79 axons and 6,914 target links. The correct source ranked above 69.46 percent of competing sources, against 59.27 percent for cohorts matched by area, layer, distance and imaging scan. The gain was 10.18 percentage points, with conditional upper-tail probability 0.001 from 999 draws. Only 4 of 79 sources ranked first. Reliability and contact opportunity controls retained positive rank gains. After removal of five shared response modes, the rank percentile was 71.41 percent against 54.18 percent. A stricter test that kept target input counts fixed had poor Markov chain mixing, with effective sample sizes of about 5 to 9. That test remains unresolved. One animal, selected axons, shared targets, coarse matching and response error limit inference. The result does not measure trial reliability, causal transmission or transfer to new animals. Original code, aggregate results, figures, hashes and external-data retrieval steps support reproduction. Source records are excluded.

display.caption: Connected target means give higher correct-source ranks than matched cohorts in one mouse. Exact identity remains difficult: 4 of 79 sources rank first. Gray ranges describe matched draws, not confidence intervals. Data credit: Ding et al. and the MICrONS Consortium (2025).

Two fixed-degree wiring chains show strong serial dependence. The stricter target-popularity test remains unresolved. These traces do not confirm convergence. Data credit: Ding et al. and the MICrONS Consortium (2025).
